questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Albania about 28,748 square kilometres; Montenegro about 13,883 square kilometres; Kosovo about 10,909 square kilometres; Cyprus about 9,242 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Tirana?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Albania is Tirana.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Albania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Albania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Albania?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Albania on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Albania article.

questions.proof: Albania is bordered by Greece, the Republic of North Macedonia, Montenegro and Kosovo.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Albania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Albania article.

questions.proof: The capital is Tirana, and other important cities are Durrës, Elbasan and Vlora.
